verdicts.text: Spacelift's paid plans scale by private worker count rather than by seats or resources, with quote-based pricing at the top end.
verdicts.evidence: Spacelift's pricing page lists every paid tier as including unlimited users, with tiers set apart by private worker count: Starter+ has 1–2, Business 3, and Enterprise "includes unlimited users and 5 to 30 private workers". Spacelift's own blog says pricing "centers on your plan and worker capacity" rather than per resource, and a 2026 Scalr comparison says Business, Enterprise and Enterprise+ are "priced on request".
verdicts.framing_note: The sources say tiers are defined by plan plus worker capacity, and paid plans include unlimited users. The claim reads that as scaling by private worker count, which is a reasonable summary. Plan features also differ between tiers.
verdicts.intuition_flag: Some third-party sites (Vendr) say pricing is by resource count, but that conflicts with Spacelift's own pages. Also, the entry paid tier Starter+ now has a published price ($20k/yr), so only the tiers above it are quote-based.

The comparison row "Workflow cost per minute / included per month" gives free as "500 free". The pricing page hero also says "Stay free forever for open source and individuals".

verdicts.text: HCP Terraform is free for up to 500 managed resources with one concurrent run, then moves to per-resource pricing of roughly $0.10 to $0.99 per resource per month depending on tier.
verdicts.evidence: HashiCorp docs: "Free plan: No charge for up to 500 managed resources." Scalr (Sep 2026) says the free tier continues "at up to 500 managed resources and one concurrent run", and paid tiers cost "$0.10, $0.47, or $0.99 per resource per month."
verdicts.framing_note: Small wording point: the Free plan has a hard cap. Going past 500 resources means switching to a paid tier, not being billed automatically. The per-resource rates come from third-party 2026 summaries. HashiCorp's own docs send readers to the pricing page for rates.

verdicts.text: Self-hosted Terraform Enterprise is available at custom pricing for larger organizations.
verdicts.evidence: Several 2025–2026 third-party pricing guides agree: ControlMonkey says "The Terraform Enterprise self-hosted pricing is custom," and env0 says TFE "comes at a custom price." HashiCorp's own pricing page came up in the search, but the snippet didn't show TFE pricing, so no first-party quote was found.
verdicts.framing_note: The sources say TFE self-hosted pricing is "custom," which matches the claim. The "for larger organizations" part is the author's own framing, and TFE's enterprise positioning supports it. AWS and Azure Marketplace list prices starting at about $15k/year, but those don't contradict custom pricing for larger deployments.

verdicts.text: Terraform's larger community reflects a decade of first-mover adoption.
verdicts.evidence: (escalated from pass1) HashiCorp says that in "July of 2014, we released Terraform 0.1, an open source, cloud-agnostic infrastructure as code solution" after noting that no one had built one since 2011. That is 12 years before today, so "a decade" of adoption and "first mover" among cloud-agnostic IaC tools both hold up. Calling the larger community a result of that head start is the author's reading, not a checkable fact.
verdicts.intuition_flag: "First-mover" only holds for cloud-agnostic IaC. CloudFormation (2011), Chef and Puppet all came before Terraform, and "a decade" slightly understates the 12 years since 2014.

verdicts.text: As measured 2026-09-21, Kubernetes has roughly 127,900 GitHub stars, Terraform roughly 49,700, OpenTofu roughly 30,200, Pulumi roughly 25,700, AWS CDK roughly 12,900, and Crossplane roughly 12,100.
verdicts.evidence: The EvanLi Github-Ranking list, updated daily, shows kubernetes at "128035" stars around 2026-09-26, which fits ~127,900 on 9/21. A Tech Insider piece from September 2026 says "Terraform sits around 49,700 stars, OpenTofu around 30,200, Pulumi around 25,700, and Crossplane on GitHub shows around 12,100." GitHub API figures from June 2026 (Terraform 48,749, OpenTofu 29,292, Pulumi 25,378) follow the same growth trend. I couldn't independently confirm AWS CDK's ~12,900.
verdicts.framing_note: The claim cites "GitHub" in general, and the numbers match third-party snapshots from the same period. The Tech Insider figures are identical to the Pulumi blog's, so that site may have copied them.
